answers.answer: SCOPe 2.08 places all three in one superfamily: Ubiquitin-like (d.15.1, SUNID 54236), inside the beta-Grasp (ubiquitin-like) fold (d.15, SUNID 54235) of class d (alpha and beta proteins, a+b). Within that superfamily they are separate families: Ubiquitin-related (d.15.1.1, SUNID 54237), UBX domain (d.15.1.2, SUNID 54250) and Ras-binding domain, RBD (d.15.1.5, SUNID 54263). The same superfamily also holds GABARAP-like, FERM first domain, APG12-like, DIX, Rho GTPase binding domain and viral protease ubiquitin-like families. The useful relationship is a shared beta-grasp scaffold and probable distant common ancestry at superfamily level. This supports structural modeling of the core fold, secondary-structure and topology expectations, and searching for remote relatives. Families are different levels of relatedness. Superfamily membership does not mean the proteins have the same biochemical function or partners. The family split reflects functional divergence: ubiquitin-related proteins include covalent modifier-type ubiquitin and ubiquitin-like domains, and UBX domains are protein-protein interaction modules, notably for p97/Cdc48 (the AAA ATPase). RBDs bind Ras-family GTPases, and the Rho GTPase binding domain family is a further separate family. Unsafe transfers: (1) Do not assume a UBX domain or RBD can be conjugated to substrates, is ubiquitin-like in the sense of being a covalent modifier, or has E1/E2/E3 or deubiquitinase interactions, because those depend on the ubiquitin C-terminal diglycine and conjugation machinery that the other families lack. (2) Do not assume a UBX domain binds p97, or that an RBD binds Ras, from fold or superfamily alone. Binding partner, surface residues, specificity and the Ras-versus-Rho-versus-other-GTPase distinction are family-specific, so a shared fold is not evidence of the same interface. (3) Do not transfer function, binding partner, localization, regulation or pathway role across families on the basis of the shared fold. A ubiquitin-like fold hit alone does not justify naming a protein a ubiquitin-like modifier, UBX protein or Ras effector. (4) Do not treat the fold or superfamily as a precise ortholog-level or family-level template relationship. Use the family-level lineage, sequence conservation and experimental evidence for function, and treat "automated matches" (d.15.1.0) as less curated. I did not examine individual domain records, so this answer rests on classification-level evidence, and the family-specific functional descriptions come from my background knowledge rather than from SCOPe.
